explanation: Hyenas sit on the cat-like side of the carnivore family tree, along with civets and mongooses. Their dog-like build evolved separately, suited to long chases and crunching bones.

claims.text: Hyenas belong to the Feliformia, the branch of carnivores that includes cats and mongooses.
Dogs, wolves, bears, raccoons, weasels and otters belong to the other branch of carnivores, the Caniformia.
Civets and mongooses are also feliform carnivores.
The dog-like body shape of hyenas evolved independently of dogs.
Spotted hyenas chase prey over long distances and can crush bones with their jaws.
